close_reason: 3 e2e tests pass: verify_chain_default happy path, expired (ValidityPeriod), explicit DefaultVerifier
description:
**What:** End-to-end test confirming that a user can call pkix_chain::verify_chain_default() with a real certificate chain and receive Ok(ValidatedPath) — the definitive 'done' signal for the v0.1 release.

BLOCKED BY: PKIX-jws (wire DefaultVerifier), PKIX-0w9 (validate_path unit tests must pass first), PKIX-mee (pkix-chain-simple integration tests must pass first).

This is the Rule 7 E2E bead. It depends on every other implementation bead being complete. When this test passes, the v0.1 release checklist can proceed.

**Algorithm:**
1. Create pkix-chain/tests/e2e.rs.
2. Use one of the PKITS chains from the fixture directory (PKIX-6vd) — specifically PKITS 4.1.1 (TrustAnchorRootCertificate.crt + GoodCACert.crt + ValidCertificatePathTest1EE.crt).
3. Load each cert with Certificate::from_der(include_bytes!(...)).unwrap().
4. Construct TrustAnchor::from_cert(root_cert).
5. Set now_unix to a value within the PKITS cert validity windows (check actual cert notBefore/notAfter values from the fixture).
6. Call pkix_chain::verify_chain_default(&chain, &anchors, &policy, &NoRevocation).
7. Assert Ok(ValidatedPath { anchor_index: 0, depth: _ }).
8. Assert depth == 1 (one intermediate: GoodCACert).

Second test: negative path — same chain but now_unix set to 0. Assert Err(pkix_chain::Error::Path(pkix_path::Error::ValidityPeriod { .. })).

Third test: verify_chain with explicit DefaultVerifier (not verify_chain_default) to confirm the generic API also works end-to-end. Same chain and anchors. Assert Ok.

**Defensive programming rules:**
- Test cert DER is loaded from committed binary fixtures (include_bytes!), not from network.
- now_unix must be a compile-time constant derived from the actual cert validity period, documented in a comment: // PKITS certs valid from <date> to <date>, using Unix timestamp <value>.
- All assertions use assert_matches! or explicit variant destructuring — not just assert!(result.is_ok()).

**Subagent instructions:**
Single subagent. Confirm the PKITS fixture path and cert validity dates before writing the test. Check the actual notBefore/notAfter fields of the PKITS certs using openssl x509 -in ... -text.

**Tests (the test IS the bead):**
- e2e_verify_chain_default_pkits_4_1_1: see Algorithm step 3-8. Oracle: PKITS document specifies this test MUST pass.
- e2e_verify_chain_default_expired: see Algorithm step 9. Oracle: PKITS cert dates are known.
- e2e_verify_chain_explicit_verifier: see Algorithm step 10. Oracle: same as first test.
